question: What does the Autel EVO Max 4N do when the control link is lost, and do incident reports match?

intake.focus: Autel EVO Max 4N lost control link behavior
intake.reason: Compare guidance/manuals and incident reports on lost control link and subsequent actions

brief.short_answer: FAA guidance indicates reestablishing the control link when lost, and if it cannot be reestablished, to start emergency or contingency procedures; preflight briefings must include control link loss procedures. The Autel EVO Max 4N manual states that on C2 link loss with automatic RTH triggered, the drone will continue to attempt reconnection; if the link is restored within 10 seconds, control returns to the remote controller; it issues real-time voice alerts; and during automated flight missions, it will keep flying in its current state until a disconnection notice is shown. Incident reports (unverified) claim loss of control shortly after takeoff, the platform flew away while attempting to return, all RTH attempts failed, and the UAS has not been located.
